title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Union spaces for studying, making, attending campus events, and connecting with other students.

cards.title: Reamer Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Student services, dining, WRUC, and Concordiensis
cards.notes: Use Reamer as a practical between-class stop: meet collaborators, visit student-resource offices, or check the posted activity around the building.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building that combines student services, food, media, and informal gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: Union identifies Reamer as home to student offices, dining services, WRUC, and Concordiensis, with a back patio used for lunch and studying.
cards.access_notes: Located on Union’s campus; dining, offices, and other services have their own availability and requirements.

cards.title: Schaffer Library Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, first floor
cards.notes: Bring a research question or group assignment and choose the Learning Commons when conversation and shared work fit better than a silent floor.
cards.short_summary: A student-focused library area for independent and collaborative research.
cards.evidence_claim: Union describes the Learning Commons as a student-focused area supporting independent and collaborative research.
cards.access_notes: Library entry requires a current Union College ID; use the library’s posted hours and study-zone guidance.

cards.title: Nott Memorial
cards.subtitle: Mandeville and Wikoff galleries; campus event space
cards.notes: Check the event and gallery listings before heading inside; the building also has third-floor sitting areas for a quieter reading break.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark used for talks, readings, special events, gallery viewing, and study.
cards.evidence_claim: Union states that the Nott hosts talks, readings, special events, Mandeville Gallery exhibitions, and third-floor study seating near the Wikoff Student Gallery.
cards.access_notes: Event and gallery access can vary; confirm the relevant campus listing before visiting.

cards.title: Jackson's Garden
cards.subtitle: Eight-acre campus garden
cards.notes: Take a short reset along the creek or gazebo, then bring a sketchbook, book, or picnic for a low-key outdoor break between commitments.
cards.short_summary: A campus garden with paths, plants, sculptures, a creek, and a gazebo.
cards.evidence_claim: Union describes Jackson’s Garden as an eight-acre garden where students sketch, paint, picnic, practice yoga, and read.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and seasonal access apply; enter through the campus garden entrance and respect the landscape.

cards.title: Old Chapel
cards.subtitle: Language Center, International Programs, and event space
cards.notes: Look for public campus programs here, or use a scheduled Language Center visit to practice with the resources and conversation support available upstairs.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus building that brings together student resources, events, language learning, and international-program support.
cards.evidence_claim: Union says Old Chapel hosts campus events and contains International Programs and the Language Center, which supports language learning and conversation partners.
cards.access_notes: Language Center appointments and event access vary; check the relevant office or event information first.

cards.title: Feigenbaum Center for Visual Arts
cards.subtitle: Studios, galleries, and maker resources
cards.notes: Visit an exhibition or attend a listed art talk, then ask the department about course-linked studios and maker resources before planning project work.
cards.short_summary: A visual-arts building with studios, exhibition spaces, and hands-on making facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Union lists drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography, digital-arts, and maker facilities in the Feigenbaum Center for Visual Arts.
cards.source_title: Visual Arts Facilities and Resources | Union College
cards.access_notes: Studio and equipment use may be tied to courses or department permissions; gallery and event availability varies.

cards.title: Crowell and West Galleries
cards.subtitle: Feigenbaum Center for Visual Arts
cards.notes: Watch the visual-arts calendar for exhibitions, artist talks, workshops, or receptions, and give yourself time to view the student and professional work closely.
cards.short_summary: Paired gallery spaces that present professional-artist and student exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Union reports that the Crowell and West Galleries host professional and student exhibitions and regularly host receptions, workshops, and artist talks.
cards.source_title: Visual Arts Facilities and Resources | Union College
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions and events change during the academic year; verify the current visual-arts schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Henle Dance Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Theater and Dance performance venue
cards.notes: Use the current-season calendar to find a studio performance, master class, lecture-demonstration, or discussion that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus dance venue hosting performances and program events.
cards.evidence_claim: Union’s current Theater and Dance season lists performances and campus events in Henle Dance Pavilion, including master classes and lecture-demonstrations.
cards.source_title: Current Season | Theater & Dance | Union College
cards.access_notes: Admission and participation vary by event; review the current-season listing for the specific program.

cards.title: Wold Student Gallery
cards.subtitle: Peter Irving Wold Center, first floor
cards.notes: Pair a pass through the Wold Center with time to view the student work on display, then follow Visual Arts announcements for changing exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor gallery where Union student artists exhibit work.
cards.evidence_claim: Union states that the Wold Student Gallery displays work by annual Visual Arts prize winners and other student artists for weeks to months.
cards.source_title: Visual Arts Facilities and Resources | Union College
cards.access_notes: Artwork rotates; check Visual Arts communications for current exhibition details.

cards.title: Kenney Community Center
cards.subtitle: Community engagement and outreach
cards.notes: Start with the center’s current opportunities if you want a structured way to connect a campus interest with a Schenectady-area volunteer commitment.
cards.short_summary: A Union center connected to student volunteer activity and community outreach.
cards.evidence_claim: Union identifies the Kenney Community Center as part of its community outreach work and reports student involvement in its volunteer activities.
cards.source_title: Four students honored for volunteer service | Union College
cards.access_notes: Volunteer opportunities and participation requirements vary; contact the center for current options.
